# I had an AI build a construction photo log: components made for photo management worked almost unchanged for construction records (build log #175)

> **Build log series**: I hand my own design system `@gunjo/ui` ([Gunjo](https://gunjo.jp)) to an AI that has never seen it, and have it build real screens. This is the second construction screen. The brief: a **construction photo log screen for a site supervisor**. It brings together a list of photos linked to the date taken, type of work, and location, along with filters, an enlarged view, before-and-after correction photos from inspections, and photo selection for reports.

## Result: 4/5. The photo management components worked unchanged for a construction photo log

I gave an AI that had never seen Gunjo nothing but the public npm package and the gunjo.jp docs, and asked it to build the screen. `tsc` passed clean, and the screen works on both mobile and desktop.

The highlight is that **components added to Gunjo for photo management (digital asset management) worked almost unchanged for a construction photo log**. They were intended for managing an asset library, but they became the main components in a photo log from a different industry.

- **`AssetGrid` (photo grid)**: it lays out thumbnails, supports multiple selection, and provides a place (`renderMeta`) to add badges for the type or stage of work beneath each photo. It fit the log grid particularly well.
- **`AssetInspectorPanel` (detail panel)**: it accepts arbitrary fields, comments, and classification tags, so the construction photo board details (project name, type of work, survey point, and date taken) could appear unchanged in a desktop side panel.
- **`MediaPickerDialog` (multiple-selection dialog)**: it matched the report workflow of "build a log from the selected photos" unchanged.
- **`FileUploader` (upload)**: it already covers accepted file types, file count, size, and progress, so it matched photo intake completely.

The photo grid, filtering, upload, and report selection all came together from existing components alone.

## What was missing: construction photo board details in the enlarged view and before-and-after correction photos

Two areas remained uncovered, and both have a clear scope.

1. **The enlarged view cannot show the construction photo board details.** The lightbox for enlarging a single image (`MediaLightbox`) is already polished, with zoom, previous and next navigation, and support for portrait images, but **the information shown beside it is fixed to file attributes (dimensions, type, size, creation date, and rating)**. A construction photo needs work information such as the type of work, survey point, location, and comments, but there is no place to pass that in. This time I hand-rolled the enlarged view. The lightbox itself works well, so this gap would close if it could accept work-specific details.
2. **There is no component for showing correction photos as a pair.** I wanted to place the before and after photos side by side for an issue found during an inspection, but there is no component for that. Similar components exist, but none are meant for comparing the same subject before and after a correction. I hand-rolled this part too.

The hand-rolled portion was about 140 lines out of roughly 900 for the whole screen, so it was only one part. Most of the screen came together by composing existing components. I follow the rule of three: a missing component gets built for real only after three separate screens have needed it independently. These two are still at one.

## Where the names and entry points got confusing

- **The name `Gallery` is confusing.** It sounds like a grid of photos, but the component is actually a single-item viewer with one large image and a strip of thumbnails. `AssetGrid` is the grid for a photo log. I almost chose `Gallery` first and took a detour.
- **The by-use-case table has no entry for photo, image, or media management.** The photo management components at the center of this screen could not be reached through the by-use-case table, a static table that maps what you want to build to the components for it. I found them only after reading the type definitions. Someone who starts from the use case of building a photo screen cannot reach the main components. There is room to improve that guidance.

## Wrapping up

The skeleton of the second construction screen also came together unchanged from components built for another purpose. Components prepared for photo management became the main parts of a construction photo log in a different industry. The only areas left uncovered were showing work-specific details in the enlarged view and comparing photos before and after a correction, two needs specific to this screen. Once again, the components that work in common cover a broad area, while the missing pieces cluster around industry-specific needs.
